title.narrative: Improving the Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics Secondary Education Project

description.narrative: The project aims to build a human capital base to support Tajikistan's transition to higher labor productivity and competitiveness. It will strengthen gender-inclusive access to quality secondary education in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) subjects and develop climate change awareness among the country's secondary school graduates. The project proposes to modernize teaching, upgrade the learning environment, improve school management, introduce and integrate climate change education, and expand girls' participation in STEM studies and women's career paths toward high-productivity sectors.

description.narrative: Learning outcome of secondary education students on STEM subjects and their preparedness for tackling climate change impacts improved

42% of grade 9 completers (43% F) reached at least basic level of competency in applying sciences and mathematics knowledge to ‘real world' situations Progress/Status: The first round of assessment will be done in Q1 2029 Data Source: Survey on applying sciences and mathematics knowledge to ‘real world' situations Baseline value: Less than 40%

At least 1 percentage point increase in the proportion of grade 11 completers (at least 0.5 percentage point higher for girls) registered in Cluster 1 in the national tests Progress/Status: The first tracer study is ongoing. A firm has been selected, and a contract was signed with LLC “Akademiyai rushdi ijtimoi” on 24 February 2026. The firm is currently developing a detailed Inception Report Data Source: Annual project progress report by the project administration group, National Testing Center report Baseline value: 11.1%

At least 50% of grade 9 female completers assessed at school with IT competency and are aware of basic climate change resilience practices Progress/Status: The first round of assessment will be done in Q1 2029 Data Source: Surveys on students' IT competency and their understanding of climate change Baseline value: 42.9%
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Climate change education and disaster resilience capacity enhanced Indicator: 450 teachers and teacher trainers (45% F) on STEM trained on climate change (2023 baseline: NA, 39.1% of STEM teachers are F) (OP 2.1.1, OP 3.2.2) Progress/Status: As of March 2026. A training program on STEM and climate change is under development and will continue as part of ongoing capacity-building efforts. Data Source: Quarterly project progress report by PAG Actual value:

Output: Climate change education and disaster resilience capacity enhanced Indicator: 5 representative schools* (4 in rural areas), reconstructed and/or provided with STEM blocks and sex-segregated WASH facilities compliant with climate change risk and disaster risk resilience including seismic proofing requirements (2023 Baseline: these school facilities not climate and disaster risk-resilient) (OP 2.4.1, OP 3.2.5) Progress/Status: As of March 2026. The construction is ongoing in an active phase across 10 target schools. Progress of civil works by package is as follows: CW01: Secondary School No. 4 (Dangara) - 28%, No. 35 (Vahdat) - 26%, No. 3 (Muminobod) - 25%, No. 8 (Kulob) - 21% CW02: Secondary School No. 16 (Vose) - 30%, No. 67 (Dangara) - 18%, No. 19 (Mir Said Ali Hamadoni) - 16% CW06: Secondary School No. 4 (Mastchoh) - 15%, No. 32 (Panjakent) - 16%, No. 2 (Khorugh) - 14% Data Source: Quarterly project progress report by PAG Actual value:

Output: Climate change education and disaster resilience capacity enhanced Indicator: 80 community awareness-raising events on climate change held (50% audience are F) (2023 Baseline: NA; 49.7% population are F) (OP 2.5.1, OP 3.2.2) Progress/Status: As of March 2026. To support the implementation of community awareness-raising activities on climate change, an international consultant conducted a training on climate change issues for selected representatives of the MoES, the TSPU and a Pedagogical college. The training strengthened participants' capacity to deliver climate change awareness activities at the community level, with a focus on gender-responsive approaches. Data Source: Survey of participants' satisfaction Actual value:

Output: Climate change education and disaster resilience capacity enhanced Indicator: At least 5 gender-responsive climate change modules developed and provided for updating curricula, and adopted in TLMs and in the pilot pre-service teacher education program (2023 Baseline: NA) Progress/Status: As of March 2026. Climate change materials to be included in TLMs have been developed for Grade 5 Chemistry and Biology. Development for other subjects and grades is ongoing. Data Source: (i) Clearance by the Research Center under the Academy of Education, and approval by MOES; (ii) endorsement by the RTMC, clearance by the Higher Education Department, and approval by MOES; and (iii) quarterly project progress report by PAG Actual value:

Output: Learning environment improved Indicator: 15 selected schools, including 14 in rural areas, provided with climate risk and disaster risk-resilient and energy-efficient STEM blocks and classrooms, and sex-segregated WASH facilities (2023 Baseline: these schools need emergency repair or reconstruction, and lack WASH facilities) Progress/Status: As of March 2026. The preparation of detailed design and cost estimate documentation for the construction of additional STEM blocks in 20 target schools has been fully completed and approved by the State Expertise. The construction is ongoing in an active phase across 10 target schools. Progress of civil works by package is as follows: CW01: Secondary School No. 4 (Dangara) - 28%, No. 35 (Vahdat) - 26%, No. 3 (Muminobod) - 25%, No. 8 (Kulob) - 21% CW02: Secondary School No. 16 (Vose) - 30%, No. 67 (Dangara) - 18%, No. 19 (Mir Said Ali Hamadoni) - 16% CW06: Secondary School No. 4 (Mastchoh) - 15%, No. 32 (Panjakent) - 16%, No. 2 (Khorugh) - 14% Data Source: Quarterly project progress report by PAG Actual value:

Output: Learning environment improved Indicator: 20 selected schools, including 18 in rural areas, equipped with modern science laboratories and ICT facilities backed up with stable electricity solutions and installed with heat pumps (2023 Baseline: these schools lack science laboratories and ICT facilities, run power outages, and lack clean heating) Progress/Status: As of March 2026. The specifications for the laboratory equipment are now under review and discussion. Data Source: Quarterly project progress report by PAG Actual value:

Output: Quality of STEM education improved Indicator: 450 in-service STEM teachers and teacher trainers (45% F) trained on skills-based approach, STEM subjects and/or cross-subjects, using laboratory practical application (2023 Baseline: no such training systematically, 39.1% of 386 in-service STEM teachers are F) Progress/Status: As of March 2026. HRDT plan discussed, drafted and submitted. From 12 January to 3 February 2026, over 250 teachers, school leaders from target secondary schools, and representatives from regional education departments participated in training on the competency- and skills-based approach, organized and conducted by the PAG. The sessions introduced participants to modern pedagogical methods, interactive approaches, and best practices, familiarizing them with the new methodology. Data Source: Quarterly project progress report by PAG Actual value:

Output: Quality of STEM education improved Indicator: Gender-responsive TLMs on grades 5 to 11 STEM subjects updated in line with skills-based approach, and 20 digital libraries on STEM subjects, available for all STEM teachers and students in project schools (2023 Baseline: TLMs outdated and not available for all teachers and students, no digital library) Progress/Status: As of March 2026. The TLM guide has been developed and is currently under MoES review. Following MoES order No.210 (18 Feb 2026), a selection committee was established to recruit developers of supplementary TLMs for Grades 5-11. After reviewing applications and conducting interviews (18-20 Feb 2026), 64 specialists were selected and organized into working groups for six subjects: Physics, Chemistry, IT, Geography, Biology, and Mathematics. From 11 to 18 March 2026, training on new methods for creating competency-based TLMs was conducted for the working groups under the guidance of national and international experts.
Data Source: Quarterly project progress report by PAG Actual value:

Output: Climate change education and disaster resilience capacity enhanced Indicator: Detailed model designs of general secondary school buildings on climate change risk and disaster risk resilience including seismic proofing developed and endorsed (2023 Baseline: national building codes have seismic proofing but no climate change risk or other disaster risk resilience requirements) (OP 3.2.5) Progress/Status: Completed As of March 2026. Detailed design and cost estimate documentation for the construction of additional STEM blocks in 20 target schools, incorporating climate- and disaster-resilient, energy-efficient STEM blocks and classrooms, as well as sex-segregated WASH facilities, has been fully completed and approved by the State Expertise. Data Source: Approval by the MOES Baseline year: 2023 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2023 Baseline value: N Target year: 2029 Target value: Y

Output: Female-friendly STEM education system promoted Indicator: 16 new labs and learning spaces reconstructed or built, 2 WASH facilities built and 2 female dormitory buildings at TSPU and DPC renovated (2023 Baseline: labs inadequate and outdated for STEM, lack of WASH facilities and dormitories in need of repair) Progress/Status: As of March 2026. Not yet started. Data Source: Quarterly project progress report by PAG; GAP monitoring Baseline year: 2023 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2023 Baseline value: N Target year: 2029 Target value: Y

Output: Female-friendly STEM education system promoted Indicator: 600 female STEM teacher candidates newly enrolled in TSPU and DPC received scholarships, 600 schoolgirls from grades 9-11 at the project schools received stipends, and 50 in-service female STEM teachers at the project schools received research assistantships (2023 Baseline: No scholarship specialized on STEM, no such stipends or assistantships) Progress/Status: As of March 2026. The Gender Operational Manual and the Regulation on the Scholarship and Incentive Program have been developed. The Gender Operational Manual is currently under review by MoES, while the Regulation was approved by MoES on 17 December 2025. The Regulation outlines all mechanisms and rules for providing stipends and incentives, including the complete stipend payment process for school students, university students, and teachers. A series of meetings were conducted in target schools, TSPU, and DPC with students, university students, teachers, and parents to raise awareness about the programs. Data Source: Quarterly project progress report by PAG; GAP monitoring Baseline year: 2023 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2023 Baseline value: N Target year: 2029 Target value: Y

Output: Female-friendly STEM education system promoted Indicator: Additional courses in reproductive health and rights for secondary school students developed and implemented for 2,000 secondary school female students from grade 9 to 11; and an ICT-based women's leadership course developed and implemented for 1,000 female teachers and teacher candidates (2023 Baseline: NA) (OP 2.2.3, OP 2.3.1) Progress/Status: As of March 2026. Development of modules on women's leadership, reproductive health and SEAH is ongoing by the contractor LLC “Alomat” Data Source: Endorsement by the RTMC and approval by MOES; Quarterly project progress report by PAG; GAP monitoring Baseline year: 2023 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2023 Baseline value: N Target year: 2029 Target value: Y

Output: Female-friendly STEM education system promoted Indicator: Advanced ICT courses including English language training provided for 1,000 secondary school STEM teachers and teacher candidates (52% F) (2023 Baseline: ICT and formal English for special purposes taught only in informatics and math program with an intake at TSPU of 326 students [46.6% F]) (OP 2.2.1) Progress/Status: As of March 2026. For the implementation of ICT courses under Package CS07, “Selection of a Company for ICT Program Development and Training,” LLC “Academy of Social Development” was selected, and a contract was signed on 26 December 2025, which includes the development and implementation of the ICT-based course. Development of ICT-based courses is ongoing by LLC LLC “Akademiyai rushdi ijtimoi” Data Source: Endorsement by the RTMC, clearance by the Higher Education Department, and approval by MOES; Quarterly project progress report by PAG; GAP monitoring Baseline year: 2023 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2023 Baseline value: N Target year: 2029 Target value: Y

Output: Female-friendly STEM education system promoted Indicator: STEM extracurricular activities offered at schools, including career orientation guidance for 7,000 secondary school students (50% F) (2023 Baseline: NA, 45.2% F) Progress/Status: As of March 2026. Development of STEM extracurricular activities is ongoing. In addition, five modules on career orientation guidance have been completed, while the remaining two modules, including those on climate change, are still under development. Data Source: Quarterly project progress report by PAG; GAP monitoring Baseline year: 2023 Baseline value: 0 Target year: 2029 Target value: 50%

Output: Quality of STEM education improved Indicator: E-learning platform established and operational for in-service STEM teachers' continuous professional development (2023 Baseline: teachers trained once every 5 years for re-accreditation training only, and e-platform unavailable) (OP 1.1) Progress/Status: As of March 2026. The concept of the e-learning platform was developed by the contractor - LLC “Iqtidor”, and approved by the MOES. The platform is now under development. Data Source: Quarterly project progress report by PAG Baseline year: 2023 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2023 Baseline value: N Target year: 2029 Target value: Y

Output: Quality of STEM education improved Indicator: School-level exams on STEM enriched with test items in line with skills-based approach (2023 Baseline: no such test item exists) Progress/Status: As of March 2026. School-level STEM exams were briefly discussed during the meetings PISF firm with RIITT and RMTC. Data Source: School-level exam samples; Quarterly project progress report by PAG Baseline year: 2023 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2023 Baseline value: N Target year: 2029 Target value: Y

Output: School-level management strengthened Indicator: 10 MOES staff and 26 local education department staff (50% F), 20 school heads and 100 STEM teachers (40% F) trained on reporting and analyzing SIS data based on new functions (2023 Baseline: No such training as functions are new, 10% of school heads are F, 39.1% of STEM teachers are F) (OP 2.1.1, OP 6.1.1) Progress/Status: As of March 2026. Not started yet. Data Source: Survey of trainees' satisfaction, quarterly project progress report by PAG Baseline year: 2023 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2023 Baseline value: N Target year: 2029 Target value: Y

Output: School-level management strengthened Indicator: SIS enabled with functions to report on individual students' attendance, dropout and learning results (2023 Baseline: no electronic system exists at school level and students' school assessment results are only recorded on paper and not reported per student; EMIS lacks such functions) (OP 6.1) Progress/Status: As of March 2026. The ToR and functional requirements of the SIS are currently under development in close collaboration with the MOES. Data Source: Quarterly project progress report by PAG, SIS user guide Baseline year: 2023 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2023 Baseline value: N Target year: 2029 Target value: Y
